title: Reverse Linked List
description: Walk the list once; at each node rewrite next to point at the previous node. Three pointers: prev, curr, next.

notes: Cache curr.next BEFORE rewriting curr.next = prev, otherwise you lose the rest of the list.
Return prev, not curr — curr is null at the end; prev is the new head.
Start prev = null so the original head becomes the new tail with next = null.

questions.q: Why cache curr.next before reassigning curr.next?
options: Otherwise you lose the rest of the list

questions.explain: When the loop exits, curr is null and prev points to the new head.

options: So the original head ends up with next = null (new tail)

questions.q: Space complexity of the iterative version?

blanks.hint: the new head when curr is null

L3.prompt: Write `reverseList(head)` that reverses a singly linked list. Use toList/toArr helpers and log `JSON.stringify(toArr(reverseList(toList([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]))))`.
hints: Keep three pointers: prev, curr, next.
Save curr.next first, then rewrite curr.next = prev.
